note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  New-onset left-sided throbbing headache x ~1 day with photophobia; fluctuates in intensity, improved by lying down; no nausea/vomiting, no visual changes, no focal neurologic symptoms, no fever or rash; last menstrual period ~1 week ago; on combined oral contraceptive (estrogen-containing), which is a risk factor for migraine and rare CVST.
- Relevant family medical history:  Mother with hypertension and migraines.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) — dose/route/frequency not documented; Paracetamol (acetaminophen) for headache — dose/frequency not documented. Allergy/adverse reaction: Aspirin — causes nausea (patient-reported “allergy”).
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Uses Microgynon for ~6 years; denies cyclical association with current headache; last menstrual period ~1 week ago; pregnancy status not discussed; STI history not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Alcohol: a few drinks on weekends; Tobacco: never smoker; Illicit drugs: denies.
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Reports recent work-related stress; no mood screening or self-harm risk discussed.
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Denies visual changes; photophobia present with current headache.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Lives with housemates; caring responsibilities not recorded.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (telehealth). Patient reports BP checked ~6 months ago as normal.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: First episode of significant unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia, onset on waking yesterday; no focal neurologic deficits, no fever, no neck stiffness, no nausea/vomiting. On combined oral contraceptive. Family history of migraine.
- Differential diagnoses aligned with DDx:
  - Migraine without aura (most consistent): unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, relief with rest in dark room, family history.
  - Tension-type headache (possible): recent stress, but phenotype less typical due to unilateral throbbing and photophobia.
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) (consider due to risk): on estrogen-containing OCP with new significant headache; absence of neuro deficits and improvement when lying down lowers likelihood but does not exclude early presentation.
  - SAH and viral meningitis considered low likelihood given non-thunderclap onset, no systemic or meningeal signs.
- Working diagnosis: Probable migraine without aura (first episode).
- Management priorities: Symptomatic treatment; safety-net for red flags; reassess if persistent/worsening or recurrent headaches; check blood pressure given OCP use; monitor temperature.

Management Plan

- Analgesia: Trial NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) with paracetamol/acetaminophen as advised; continue hydration and rest in a dark, quiet environment. Avoid aspirin due to reported adverse reaction (nausea).
- Safety net: Seek urgent care if headache worsens, new neurologic symptoms occur (weakness, numbness, confusion, seizures), fever develops, neck stiffness, persistent vomiting, new rash, or sudden “worst headache.”
- Monitoring: Obtain a home thermometer; check temperature if feeling unwell.
- Blood pressure: Arrange BP check soon (has not been checked in ~6 months).
- Follow-up: If headaches become persistent, recur, relate to menstrual cycle, or triggers emerge, schedule review for migraine evaluation and management options.
- Education: Discuss hydration and regular meals; minimize bright light exposure during acute episodes; consider trigger diary if recurrent.
- Considerations (given DDx): If atypical features develop (progressive severity, positional worsening when supine, visual changes, focal deficits), escalate for in-person assessment and consider neuroimaging to exclude secondary causes including CVST.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded (work stress acknowledged; no referral discussed).
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Migraine without aura — Likelihood: High. Justification: Unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, relief with rest/dark room, family history; absence of neuro deficits or systemic illness.
- Tension-type headache — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: Recent work stress and benign exam by history; less typical due to unilateral throbbing and photophobia.
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: Estrogen-containing OCP with new significant headache; currently no focal signs or progressive course.

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: BP and pulse not measured today; no height/weight/BMI/waist; no oral/ear/eye exam; no urinalysis; immunization review not done; no depression/anxiety screening; no detailed alcohol screen (AUDIT-C), caffeine intake, or sleep assessment; no pregnancy status or STI history; no cervical screening or other preventive care review; no neurological exam; no pain severity scale.
- Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality: Telehealth encounter; some sections were incomplete/inaudible; no vitals or physical exam available.
